notes: The guide's Sources note and its evidence (docs/evidence/buttongroup.md) were checked on jfs-components 0.1.60 on 24 September 2026; the installed build is 0.1.78-c1fa197 and the evidence has no later check. The installed package's own ButtonGroup doc still describes the same cascade (a child's own modes win) and stretching (non-IconButton children stretch, IconButton keeps its width), so nothing found contradicts the guide, but the pixel measurements are 0.1.60 ones. ButtonGroup reads no mode collection itself (the facts list none); mode rules target the modes prop, which reaches every child. The examples give each child only its own override and let the group's modes reach it, because the guide's Do is to set the size once on the group and the package clones group modes into every child; they do not repeat the owner's modes on each child. The guide names no other component to use instead, and has no avoid-when guidance, so avoidWhen is empty. The guide asks for one emphasized child (Pay's own Emphasis High) while its Don't warns against one child's own Button / Size; both rest on the same child-wins behaviour, and a reviewer may want the guide to say why one override is wanted and the other is not. The Sources note also records two Storybook problems, not component gaps: the default story's third icon (ic_menu) is missing from the 0.1.60 registry, and the modes story passes a token name (iconButton/background) that ButtonGroup does not read. The Figma observations were read by the orchestrator, not re-inspected by the worker that wrote the evidence.

examples.purpose: Split, request and pay in one row: the icon keeps its size, the Buttons share the rest, and only Pay sets a stronger Emphasis.
examples.jsx:
<ButtonGroup
  style={{ width: 360 }}
  modes={{ 'Color Mode': 'Light', 'Button / Size': 'M', Emphasis: 'Medium', AppearanceBrand: 'Primary' }}
>
  <IconButton iconName="ic_split" accessibilityLabel="Split bill" onPress={() => {}} />
  <Button label="Request" onPress={() => {}} modes={{ AppearanceBrand: 'Secondary' }} />
  <Button label="Pay" onPress={() => {}} modes={{ Emphasis: 'High' }} />
</ButtonGroup>

from.quote: The ButtonGroup keeps split, request, and pay together, with Pay emphasized.

evidenceFacts.name: children
evidenceFacts.description: Fragments are flattened. A direct IconButton child, checked by element type, keeps its intrinsic size; every other child (such as Button) gets flex: 1, and a wrapper component around an IconButton would stretch.
evidenceFacts.quote: A direct `IconButton` child, checked by element type, keeps its intrinsic size; a wrapper component around it would stretch.

evidenceFacts.name: modes
evidenceFacts.description: Cloned into every child; a child's explicit modes win. The group itself renders a centred row with a 12 px token gap and no padding.
evidenceFacts.quote: It flattens Fragments, clones group modes into every child (a child’s explicit modes win), and renders a centered row with the single-mode tokens `buttonGroup/gap` 12 and `buttonGroup/padding/*` 0.
